utterances.text: The way it's formulated is quite imprecise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, can you explain that, please, to the Court.

utterances.speaker: EMIN ZEBIC
utterances.text: Could you please return the Bosnian version for me. [In English] Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to be clear, are you now looking at the B/C/S, the Bosnian version?

utterances.speaker: EMIN ZEBIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes. It's all right now. It states here: "The investigation and expert work regarding the exhumation are agreed to be conducted by the crime services and the MUP." This term "MUP" means the Ministry of Internal Affairs. That's the Ministry of Internal Affairs headquartered in Sarajevo. The unit that was in Jablanica is called the Public Security Station Jablanica, and it has its own, albeit small, crimes department. That's one thing. The other thing is that we never received any request in relation to this particular item.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you have received such a request in relation to this particular item?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: My friend should clarify that, when he says "would you have received such a request," that's, in my submission, meaninglessly broad. There may be a particular form of request that he wants to say. He's in a certain line of authority. I don't object that that sort of question being asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, if you could put your question in another way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If a request had been made to -- to conduct an on-site investigation and exhumation, would your station have been involved?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry to persist in this. Your Honours, the question is a request to who in this situation. Bearing in mind the document says quite clearly that it's the -- as the witness has pointed out, it says the Sarajevo MUP is going to be involved and the Jablanica military police are going to be involved. Now, if -- my friend is allowed to ask -- he has allowed to ask, and I'm not objecting to him asking, but he's got to specify which of those two or another organ is the subject of the request that he's -- he's talking about. In other words, the line of -- the line of the request has to be made clear. That's what I'm objecting to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If there was a request to your station, where would that have come from?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm going to have to persist with the objections here. Your Honour, that's -- that has got a different problem. I don't know how the witness could ever answer where such a request would have come from. He's allowed to ask -- my friend is allowed to ask "if the army had asked your station to help, would you have helped," and that's a legitimate question to ask and that -- I wouldn't object to that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If the army had asked your station to help, would you have helped?

utterances.speaker: EMIN ZEBIC
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the army ask your station to help?

utterances.speaker: EMIN ZEBIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on the -- I want to take you to the 12th of September, 1993. Was there a Presidency war session on that day?

utterances.speaker: EMIN ZEBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you attend that session?

utterances.speaker: EMIN ZEBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was anything discussed with respect to Grabovica at that session?

utterances.speaker: EMIN ZEBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was that?

utterances.speaker: EMIN ZEBIC
utterances.text: The meeting was attended by the deputy commander of the 44th Mountain Brigade, Senad Dzino. He reported about what happened in Grabovica as the military component. And amongst other things, he said that the gentlemen from the IKM had taken upon themselves the obligation of investigating the events and taking the necessary measures. He mentioned Mr. Vehbija Karic and Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who Vehbija Karic is or did you know then who Vehbija Karic was?

utterances.speaker: EMIN ZEBIC
utterances.text: I knew that from the beginning of the war. I think that he was one of the major military authorities. I think he is of slightly lower rank than Mr. Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know whether he was in Grabovica in and around that time, in September 1993?

utterances.speaker: EMIN ZEBIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't have such information.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to show Mr. Zebic Prosecution Exhibit 156, and since it's the first time, I'll read the ERN numbers, 03639388. That's the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see -- well, firstly, do you recognise the document on your screen?

utterances.speaker: EMIN ZEBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that your signature at the bottom of the document?

utterances.speaker: EMIN ZEBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just briefly explain the content of this document, please, to the Court.

utterances.speaker: EMIN ZEBIC
utterances.text: This is a note sent to the command of the 44th Mountain Brigade on the 29th of September, 1993. During those days, we received information from soldiers and citizens that there were a number of bodies in Grabovica which were not buried and because of which there is terrible fear. That's what it says here. I wanted with this note to draw the attention of the commander of the 44th Brigade and ask them to take the most basic humane measures to have the bodies -- to give the bodies a decent burial, and I also asked them to enable a proper on-site investigation to be conducted. I would like to state that I did this because this was on territory that was not under the jurisdiction of the Jablanica Public Security Station but the command of the 44th Brigade as a part of the military structure, through the authorised higher commands would perhaps be in a position to initiate the required steps. That was the purpose of this correspondence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You told us earlier in your examination-in-chief that in addition to the 44th Mountain Brigade, the IKM, forward command post, was also located in Jablanica. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: EMIN ZEBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you told us in your examination-in-chief that Mr. Alispahic asked to be connected to the forward command post. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: EMIN ZEBIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why didn't you send this request to the forward command post?

utterances.speaker: EMIN ZEBIC
utterances.text: A rule in communications simply states that according to the vertical line, a public security station can contact its own superiors; however, when we're talking about a different structure, a military structure, then it is customary to contact those who are along the same -- who are on the same rank as we are, which in this case would be the unit or the command of the same rank. In our case, that would be the command of the 44th Mountain Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. So it's time for the break and we'll break now and -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry. I've just been advised by my case manager that I must mention that this -- this document will be MFI277, for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see. Are you going to tender them into the evidence now or at a later stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. SACHDEVA
utterances.text: If I -- if I can now, but I understand that we can do that tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, maybe we could do it tomorrow after the cross-examination. I believe the Defence has some questions to ask concerning of this document. Well, Witness, I'm afraid that we have to keep you here for another night. And as I did to all the witnesses, that I have to warn you do not talk to anybody and do not let anybody talk to you about your testimony. You understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I believe that we'll resume tomorrow afternoon. The hearing for today is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 17th day of March, 2005, at 2.15 p.m. 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.02 p.m.,
